approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, sanitizing and normalizing their identities, rejecting duplicates and submitting the first full batch allowed by its inverse-motif memory. It chooses the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move and keeps a separate best archive. Element substitutions currently change only one atom, so exchanging the positions of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon needs an intermediate graph and another round of feedback. The repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle are part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Add a direct aromatic nitrogen relocation: exchange a pyridine-like ring nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon within the same aromatic six-member ring. This changes where the nitrogen sits while retaining atom count, molecular formula, substituent attachment positions and the ring framework. The exchange becomes an additional option at either participating atom in the existing atom-change menu. Earlier siblings filtered sulfur or ring closures, removed whole branches, or assigned tetrahedral configurations; none directly moved a ring heteroatom while preserving composition. Their mechanisms are not combined with this one.

observed_bottleneck: The repaired Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 completes its full panel at mean 0.5209178281192797 and standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. Its change_atom operator alters one element at a time: moving a ring nitrogen to another position requires a separately evaluated extra-aza or deaza intermediate, even when a direct positional isomer would preserve the source formula and ring framework. Offline enumeration on all 435 saved batch-start graphs finds 92 states with an eligible aromatic six-member-ring C/N pair, 169 distinct pair opportunities, 161 nonidentity products and 160 products unseen at that state. All 169 constructed products sanitize, preserve molecular formula, atom and bond counts, bond connectivity and the qualifying ring's aromaticity, and alter exactly the two selected element identities. Among 1455 recorded change_atom draws, 26 selected a site with a relocation partner. These are unscored accessibility measurements, not predicted oracle gains. The branch-deletion sibling n-0e56e71777c4 reached compact neighbors but lost score in every seed; the configuration sibling n-3dc00c8b2932 reached new identities whose direct observed comparisons tied. They motivate a scaffold-and-formula-preserving change in heteroatom placement rather than another deletion or configuration-only proposal.
hypothesis: Extend the existing change_atom neighborhood with a direct two-site exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, producing formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers without an evaluated single-substitution intermediate.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen relocation reached ten scored positional isomers, but the panel gain missed its target
finding_summary.insights: The neighborhood extension is demonstrably usable: the ten evaluated products cannot be reached by any single legacy element substitution from their recorded sources. Unlike the earlier configuration-only experiment, nitrogen relocation changes both the motifs seen by tabu memory and the measured source scores. This rules out identity-only or score-invisible activation as the explanation for the limited panel benefit. Exposure is sparse and local outcomes are mixed: only ten of 4350 evaluated neighbors are exchanges, and most lose to their source. One selected deco_hop exchange leads into later archive improvements, but the whole walk and its random draws also change, so those later gains cannot be assigned to nitrogen placement alone. The evidence supports positional-isomer accessibility and score sensitivity, while the preregistered overall score benefit is refuted for this panel. The molecular assessment still finds the Parent-like aromatic/carbonyl families alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur and dense cages; formula conservation by itself has not established better medicinal or synthetic quality.
finding_summary.results: Ten fresh formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled exchanges. All ten changed local signed motifs; three improved their source score and seven worsened it, with no ties. Three became subsequent walk states and one immediately improved the best archive. Every sampled exchange preserved atom count, bonds, molecular formula and qualifying-ring aromaticity. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.520918 to 0.521759, a paired gain of 0.000841, below the required 0.002. One seed improved, one declined slightly and one was unchanged. The largest task change was deco_hop in the improving seed; DRD2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged in all seeds.

molecular.headline: Parent-like aromatic carbonyl and amine families retain reactive heteroatoms, unusual sulfur bonding and dense cages
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. All current proposals carry ring-closure tokens; aromatic-token rates range from 0.7184 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.2 to 69.9. The output stays within substantial ring-bearing molecules, from relatively compact indole or benzofuran carbonyl compounds to bulky decorated heterocycles, aryl amines and highly bridged sulfur-rich cages. The main leading families largely recur in the parent. There is moderate diversity across seeds but strong local concentration among closely related ring frameworks. Ordinary amides, thioethers and amines coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O connections, peroxides and multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. These strings therefore do not specify stereoisomers at possible stereogenic centres, and their neutral forms do not establish the solution ionization of basic amines. Chemical plausibility remains questionable primarily because of local bonding, ring geometry and reactivity, rather than an absence of ring or aromatic chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading benzofuran-like molecule has methyl groups, a thiol, an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro aryl amide. Another strong family is a comparatively ordinary ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. A benzothiophene-like aryl ketone with an aminomethoxy group leads the current seed-0 molecules. More bridged relatives contain O/N connections and partially saturated carbon rings; later examples introduce unusually substituted sulfur or N-N functionality. The low molecules disrupt an aromatic ring, replace the carbonyl connection or add more flexible heteroatom-rich chains. The straightforward indole and benzothiophene families are plausible synthetic starting points, while the reactive and bridged relatives are less convincing as stable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: N-Cl amides and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
N-F/N-O groups, thiols, unusual sulfur coordination and N-N connections appear in other members.
Dense ring closures and altered aromaticity can make practical synthesis and geometry uncertain.
missing_features: Low ring-expanded or carbonyl-replaced structures lack the intact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.
A systematic set of stable N-H amide and ordinary ring alternatives around the leading framework is incomplete, although several such relatives already score closely.
Substituted bridge atoms and partly saturated ring relationships remain stereochemically undefined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloro benzofuran-like amide scores 0.41003927643747895 and the ordinary indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. A bridged N-chloro amide scores 0.3923638265355735, while its N-H amide relative scores 0.3816990444462938. Conventional amide chemistry is therefore compatible with a nearby score, without proving that chlorine removal is neutral in every local context. Another bridged N-H amide family scores 0.3900523103411983 with either carbon-bound chlorine or bromine and 0.385823971421255 without that halogen. Carbonyl-replaced or ring-disrupted low examples score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.021532846118034143. The higher scores associate with compact aromatic/carbonyl organization. Parent seed 1 and seed 2 retain the same best structures and scores. Current seed 0 reaches 0.393567030299894 with the benzothiophene-like ketone, versus parental 0.3966634883331815 with a more unusual sulfur-containing framework.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are bulky decorated aryl/aza-heterocyclic compounds bearing carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, imines, an amino-fluoroalkyl connection and a long mixed ether/thioether chain. A multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centre connects another side chain; N-bromo and terminal sulfur-chlorine variants are present. The final seed-2 family instead combines a heteroaromatic dione with an unsaturated carbon chain and a fused aza/ether ring carrying acetal-like substitution. The changed seed-1 family contains a cyano-substituted amidine, heteroaromatic rings, a thioester and an O-F substituent. Recognizable fragments abound, but long flexible appendages and reactive heteroatom bonds weaken synthetic and stability plausibility.
liabilities: Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur is not an ordinary thioether or sulfone linkage.
N-Br, S-Cl and O-F bonds introduce reactive chemistry in different families.
Long mixed ether/thioether chains, unsaturation and branching increase flexibility and synthesis complexity without a demonstrated local advantage for several extensions.
missing_features: The lower altered-ring molecules lack the same retained aromatic heterocyclic organization as the stronger decorated families.
Matched simpler relatives with conventional stable linkers are incomplete; equal scores across many peripheral changes do not show a need for N-bromination, long-chain extension or additional sulfur.
Side-chain configuration, imine geometry and acetal-like centres remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated structure scores 0.6161710037174721. Multiple relatives share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite extending alkyl groups, adding side-chain branching or replacing N-methyl with N-bromo. Two final aza/ether-ring variants retain 0.6092182584436399 despite different oxygen/sulfur substitution. These ties support the main decorated aromatic/carbonyl organization more clearly than any need for those individual appendages. Early altered-ring examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063, compared with 0.548381482770623 for the initial aromatic dione. Current seed 0 and seed 2 retain the parent's leading structures and scores. Current seed 1 reaches 0.605139548855754 versus parental 0.5906482326855353, but its new amidine/thioester family includes reactive O-F chemistry rather than resolving chemical feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger products are aryl-rich polyamines with halogenated aromatic groups, phenol, primary aminomethyl substituents and saturated or partly unsaturated nitrogen rings. Sulfur-rich rings and linkers recur, including sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional carbon or nitrogen connections. Some frameworks are heavily fused and constrained. Low compounds retain carboxylic acid, amide and sulfonamide groups from the initial biaryl scaffold and have fewer readily available aliphatic amines. The aryl/amine fragments are recognizable medicinal chemistry, but the unusual sulfur valence and undefined ring relationships make the assembled molecules questionable.
liabilities: Sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds, substituted S-H centres and unusual sulfur coordination raise stability and synthesis concerns.
Small or densely fused rings add strain and require specific three-dimensional relationships.
Multiple basic centres and halogenated aromatic surface occur together without a defined solution ionization state.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives lack the accessible aliphatic-amine and linker organization of the stronger products.

Stable conventional-valence linker series preserving the same aryl and amine arrangement are incomplete. Equal carbon/sulfur comparisons show that some sulfur substitutions are optional in the observed local context.
Configurations of substituted nitrogen rings, constrained junctions and possible stereogenic sulfur environments are unassigned.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl/polyamine/sulfur-ring structure scores 0.9148143511682032. A pair differing in a fused-ring sulfur versus carbon position both score 0.8825461379136246. Another carbon/sulfur ring-connection pair both score 0.8663008496126992. Thus sulfur at those particular positions is not distinguished by the observed score. Removing the methylene from the nitrogen-to-sulfur-ring connection lowers a matched relative from 0.8663008496126992 to 0.3331237338421948, supporting a role for linker organization. Low acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives score 0.007468397818197266 to 0.011875520467584314. The same leading molecules and per-seed maxima occur in the parent: 0.8856242185485628, 0.868020189804352 and 0.9148143511682032. The molecular evidence retains both the aryl/aliphatic-amine association and the sulfur chemistry liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders combine an alkyl-substituted aza-aromatic ring, an aryl group and a polycyclic nitrogen/carbonyl framework with an N-O bridge. Closely related structures add an N-N connection, a peroxide connection or ring-size variation. Other seeds retain brominated aromatic carbonyl/thioester families or expanded mixed N/O/S carbonyl rings. The low examples open the dicarbonyl-containing ring or introduce more flexible and unusually substituted heteroatom connections, sometimes including O-Br and heavily substituted sulfur. These are substantial ring-rich molecules with familiar individual fragments but demanding assembled topology.
liabilities: N-O, N-N and O-O connections introduce labile or reactive bonds in already complex ring systems.
O-Br and unusual substituted sulfur persist in alternative families.
Expanded heterocycles and dense ring closures add conformational and synthetic uncertainty.
missing_features: The lower ring-opened molecules lack the constrained aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained in the stronger structures.
Less labile ring connections preserving that arrangement remain incompletely represented; near-equal scores for N-N, carbon and peroxide variants do not establish a need for reactive bonds.
Bridged ring relationships remain stereochemically undefined, and additional fused connections do not establish a uniquely better conformation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading alkyl-substituted bridged polycycle scores 0.21196904390980506, while a shorter substituent relative scores 0.2087472610464947 and a ring-expanded relative scores 0.2108231310031427. Alternative carbon- or nitrogen-containing connections share 0.20775769309691736, and a peroxide-containing member is close at 0.20647766243219587. The broad aromatic/carbonyl/polycyclic organization is therefore more clearly associated with the score than these unusual local bonds. Early ring-opened carbonyl-chain derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515. Current seed 0 reaches 0.21196904390980506 versus parental 0.2107445781802027 with a related phenol/nitrogen-substituted framework. Current seed 1 and seed 2 retain the same best structures and scores as the parent, 0.19092251395438758 and 0.20185639717998205, although the late seed-2 chemistry differs.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are compact but exceptionally ring-dense sulfur cages containing a nitrogen-rich dione, fluorinated carbon sites, an NH group and a sulfur-linked fluorinated alcohol substituent. Several sulfur centres are multiply bonded while additionally substituted, and S-H-containing unsaturated rings recur. Other seeds produce related cages with acyl fluoride, sulfinyl/nitrogen connections, aldehyde and N-fluoroimino functionality. Low molecules may already contain multiple rings, diones and sulfur, so these features alone do not distinguish success. The chemistry remains highly questionable despite moderate overall size.
liabilities: Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur and unsaturated S-H rings are difficult stability and synthesis features.
Acyl fluoride, N-F, sulfur-halogen and aldehyde groups occur in alternative cages.
Very dense ring connections can imply severe geometric constraints even when the SMILES parses successfully.
missing_features: The weaker rearrangements do not preserve the specific carbonyl and fluorinated-substituent arrangement present in the stronger cage relatives.

The displayed leading series lacks conventional-valence, less constrained ring alternatives retaining those local features. The scores do not establish that unusual sulfur coordination or dense cages are chemically necessary.
Substituted fluorinated centres and cage junctions are stereochemically unspecified, with no demonstrated accessible configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated dione cage scores 0.5903526424693334. A related carbonyl-containing cage scores 0.519850349488241, versus 0.48440391849409126 when the displayed carbonyl is replaced by imino functionality. Other ring variants retain 0.5486087229725075 or 0.5527071687189122, indicating that exact connectivity matters within the family. Early expanded aromatic diones and sulfur-rich frameworks score 7.590554525032884e-10 and 1.0546805269255595e-09. In seed 2, the compact carbonyl/aldehyde cage scores 0.4484554129767839, while an expanded oxygen/carbonyl-ring variant scores 0.2536619453071564. The leading structures and per-seed best scores are the same as the parent: 0.48118636011729826, 0.5903526424693334 and 0.4484554129767839. Thus the observed molecular evidence preserves the same carbonyl/fluorinated-cage associations and unresolved chemical feasibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited output includes N-halogen, O-halogen, peroxide and N-N/N-O connections, as well as sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and additionally substituted sulfur. A conventional indole amide scores 0.39905049777278273, and matched carbon/sulfur variants share 0.8825461379136246 or 0.8663008496126992.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful aryl, amine and carbonyl arrangements are still coupled to reactive heteroatom bonds and unusual sulfur valence.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable matched linkers and heteroatom substitutions while retaining useful fragment placement. Distinguish ordinary sulfur functional groups and carbon-bound halogens from unusual sulfur coordination and reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several decorated heterocycles share 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension, branching or N-methyl-to-N-bromo substitution. Carbon/nitrogen connection variants share 0.20775769309691736, while a peroxide relative remains close at 0.20647766243219587. These observations do not establish a need for the extra reactive bonds or flexible appendages.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically simpler alternatives remain incomplete where local appendage changes are indistinguishable or nearly indistinguishable in score.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include matched simplifications that reduce unnecessary branches, reactive connections and flexible side chains while preserving the principal molecular framework. Use observed feedback to decide which simpler chemistry retains the useful arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Removing a methylene from a nitrogen-to-sulfur-ring connection changes a displayed score from 0.8663008496126992 to 0.3331237338421948. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain compounds score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, below related constrained aromatic/carbonyl structures. Altering aromaticity or carbonyl placement can matter even when ring and heteroatom content remain high.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring and linker changes do not consistently preserve the arrangement associated with stronger scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate coherent matched variations in linker length, ring size and polar-group attachment while retaining the other useful features. Broaden access to ordinary feasible ring systems without indiscriminately opening, enlarging or densely closing rings.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre-token rate 0.0. The displayed structures include substituted saturated rings, N/O bridges, fluorinated carbon sites and densely connected sulfur cages. Several leading molecules are the same unassigned structures present in the parent.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity and geometric feasibility remain undefined for constrained products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Specify feasible configurations where stereogenic relationships exist and preserve them through structural changes. Pair this with less constrained ring alternatives; an aromatic token or successful parse does not establish a realizable three-dimensional molecule.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
